_doc: Labeled COVERAGE calibration set for tuning the fact-checker's coverage judge. Each item: does NARRATION convey FACT? conveyed=true when a listener would learn the fact even if reworded/paraphrased; false when the fact is absent or contradicted. Drawn from REAL tour narrations (Palais de Justice, Notre-Dame, Conciergerie, Hotel-Dieu — author-engine + stitch outputs) so the judge is calibrated on the actual paraphrase gap that broke convergence. Positives are paraphrases the strict entailer WRONGLY rejected; negatives are genuine drops.

items.fact: The kings of France never returned to the island.
items.narration: One night he slipped out along the river, resettled in the Marais, then walled himself inside the Louvre — and no king of France came back to this island again.
items.note: paraphrase: 'never returned' == 'no king came back again'

items.fact: Jean II le Bon was being held captive in England.
items.narration: King Jean le Bon sat captive in England, the Valois dynasty barely begun, and the provost of merchants dreamed of toppling the crown.

items.fact: The young Dauphin, the future Charles V, was sitting in the palace with two of his counsellors when Marcel's men burst in and slew the counsellors before his eyes.
items.narration: So his men burst in on the young Dauphin, the future Charles the Wise, and cut down two of his counsellors where he sat.

items.fact: During the Revolution, 2,278 victims of the Revolutionary Tribunal passed through this arcade on their way out, to the jeers of delighted tricoteuses huddled on the perron.
items.narration: During the Revolution, two thousand two hundred and seventy-eight condemned passed through it, out to the jeers of knitting women on the steps.

items.fact: The Emmanuel Bell was forged in 1685.
items.narration: Above them hangs Emmanuel, forged in 1685.

items.fact: Marie, the great bell of the north tower, was destroyed and melted down.
items.narration: When the Revolution came in 1789, it spared him — but his sister, Marie, in the north tower, they melted down.

items.fact: In medieval times there were three people per bed — one sick, one dying, and one dead.
items.narration: Beds held three at once — one sick, one dying, one dead.

items.fact: The Hotel-Dieu is the oldest public hospital in Paris.
items.narration: This is the oldest public hospital in Paris, founded in 651 by Bishop Saint-Landry.

items.fact: The moat and drawbridge that defended this palace proved useless on 22 February 1357.
items.narration: The moat and the drawbridge were supposed to keep danger out; on the twenty-second of February, 1357, they kept nothing at all.
items.note: 'proved useless' == 'kept nothing at all'; date spelled out

items.fact: The Salle des Gens d'Armes was built between 1301 and 1315.
items.narration: In the vast Salle des Gens d'Armes, raised between 1301 and 1315, an iron grille penned the poor who slept on straw.

items.fact: Prisoners were tortured in the westernmost tower, the Tour Bonbec.
items.narration: Look up at that westernmost tower facing the Seine, and imagine what once carried across the water. Screams.
items.note: torture conveyed via 'screams'; tower named later in the stop

items.fact: The Dauphin moved to the Hotel de Saint-Pol in the Marais.
items.narration: One night he slipped out along the river, resettled in the Marais, then walled himself inside the Louvre.
items.note: REAL DROP: 'Hotel de Saint-Pol' name is not conveyed (only 'the Marais')

items.fact: The Dauphin spent time at the Louvre from 1368 onward.
items.narration: One night he slipped out along the river, resettled in the Marais, then walled himself inside the Louvre.
items.note: REAL DROP: the '1368' date is absent

items.fact: The arcade was the entrance to the Conciergerie before 1825.
items.narration: Look right, to that arcade off the Cour de Mai.
items.note: REAL DROP: 'entrance to the Conciergerie before 1825' not conveyed

items.fact: The Emmanuel Bell weighs thirteen tons.
items.narration: Above them hangs Emmanuel, forged in 1685, one of Europe's oldest bells.
items.note: REAL DROP: the 'thirteen tons' weight is absent

items.fact: The cathedral's other nine bells were replaced in 2013.
items.narration: Emmanuel still rings for Christmas, for great occasions, and for grief.
items.note: REAL DROP: nothing about the nine bells or 2013

items.fact: Etienne Marcel was the provost of merchants.
items.narration: the provost of merchants, Etienne Marcel, dreamed of toppling the crown with English help.

items.fact: Jean II le Bon was the founder of the Valois dynasty.
items.narration: King Jean le Bon sat captive in England, the Valois dynasty barely begun.
items.note: REAL DROP: 'barely begun' does NOT state Jean FOUNDED the Valois dynasty

items.fact: The Conciergerie is Paris's oldest prison, where Marie-Antoinette was held before execution.
items.narration: You stand at the oldest prison in Paris, a vestige of the medieval Palais de Justice. Here Marie-Antoinette waited.

items.fact: Two oubliettes spiked with iron and connected to the river were found during an 1828 restoration.
items.narration: Then, during an 1828 restoration, workers opened two oubliettes — hidden dungeons spiked with iron, connected to the river.

items.fact: The rose windows are coloured in imperial purple.
items.narration: That light pours through transept walls that are nearly two-thirds glass, and through two rose windows glowing imperial purple.

items.fact: The bell only rings at Christmas, special occasions, or in times of mourning.
items.narration: Emmanuel still rings for Christmas, for great occasions, and for grief.

items.fact: Napoleon crowned himself emperor here in 1804.
items.narration: The moat and drawbridge proved useless in 1357, and the young Dauphin fled by the river.
items.note: REAL DROP: nothing about Napoleon or 1804 (contradiction-free absence)

items.fact: The chapel houses a piece of the True Cross and the Crown of Thorns.
items.narration: Louis paid a fortune for the relics, more than the chapel itself cost.
items.note: REAL DROP: 'relics' mentioned but the specific True Cross / Crown of Thorns not conveyed
